messages.content: I need to sort out Chicago for the university-press rights conference in late March. It runs Thursday through Sunday, and I need both a flight from Denver and a hotel near the conference.

What are the dates and the conference venue? I also need the Thursday briefing time, when your Denver commitment ends, and the ending time on Sunday so I can compare complete combinations rather than isolated fares.

The conference is March 26 through March 29 at the Palmer House. I have to be in our Denver office Thursday morning and cannot leave before 10:30. The exhibitor briefing starts at 5:30 p.m. Thursday. The final session ends at 12:30 Sunday, and I should stay through it.

That makes Thursday the tighter side. Are you able to leave directly for DEN at 10:30, and will you have checked luggage or only a carry-on? For Sunday, is there a latest acceptable arrival in Denver?

I can go straight to the airport, but realistically I would not reach the terminal before about 11:15. Carry-on only. On Sunday I would like to be home that evening, though I do not need the earliest possible flight.

Understood. I will treat departures before noon Thursday as impractical. Since the Palmer House is in the Loop, I will check both airports: Midway is often quicker to the venue, while O'Hare generally has more nonstop choices. Do you have a room budget or any hotel requirements for this trip?
Try to keep the room under $250 a night before tax. It is just me, so one bed is fine. I mainly care about a straightforward walk to the conference and a room where I can work.

I found three workable hotel candidates for Thursday through Sunday. The Palmer House itself is about $239 nightly, roughly $838 including estimated taxes for three nights. The Silversmith, about a two-minute walk away, is approximately $219 nightly or $768 with taxes. Staypineapple Chicago is about an eight-minute walk and comes to roughly $705 total at a $199 nightly base rate. All three list a desk and in-room Wi-Fi. Shall I prioritize the shortest walk, or is the lower total at Staypineapple worth considering?
Keep all three for now. Being in the conference hotel could save time, but I am not sure it is worth another $130 over Staypineapple. What flights actually get me there safely?

The strongest Thursday options I found are: a Southwest nonstop leaving DEN at 12:05 p.m. and reaching MDW at 3:25 p.m. for $238 round trip with a Sunday return; a United nonstop leaving at 12:10 and reaching ORD at 3:39 for $276 round trip; and an American nonstop leaving at 12:45 and reaching ORD at 4:14 for $251 round trip. The first two provide reasonable buffers. The American option leaves little room for a delay because travel from O'Hare to the Palmer House can take an hour or more in late-afternoon traffic.
Drop the American flight. For the other two, what Sunday returns work after the 12:30 session?

Southwest has a 3:50 p.m. nonstop from MDW arriving DEN at 5:35 p.m. United has a 4:35 p.m. nonstop from ORD arriving at 6:20. Both allow time to leave the Palmer House after the session. Midway is typically 25 to 40 minutes by car from the Loop at that hour; for O'Hare I would allow about an hour, so the United schedule is comfortable but does not leave much time for a long lunch.
Can you lay out the best complete combinations and include airport transportation? I want to see the real difference, not just room rates.

Here are three sensible packages using current quoted prices and estimated ground transportation. Combination A: Southwest through MDW plus Staypineapple, about $238 airfare, $705 hotel, and $80 total for two rideshares, approximately $1,023 overall. Combination B: Southwest plus the Silversmith, about $1,086 overall using the same ground estimate. Combination C: United through ORD plus the Palmer House, about $276 airfare, $838 hotel, and roughly $120 for two rideshares, approximately $1,234 overall. The conference hotel with the Midway flight would be about $1,156, so airport and hotel choices can be mixed.
Is public transit practical from Midway on Thursday, or would I be making the afternoon too tight?

It is practical if the flight is on time. The Orange Line from Midway to the Loop takes roughly 30 to 35 minutes, followed by a short walk, but deplaning and reaching the station add time. A 3:25 arrival would likely put you at the hotel between 4:25 and 4:45. That leaves enough time to check in and reach a 5:30 briefing. A rideshare could be faster in light traffic, but roadway congestion makes it less predictable. I would use the train unless the flight arrives materially late.
That makes the Southwest option more appealing. Please compare the three hotels a little more closely for getting to morning sessions and doing some work Thursday night.

Palmer House is the easiest operationally: no outdoor commute, and you can return to the room between sessions. Its standard rooms can be compact, but they include a work surface. Silversmith is across the street on Wabash, about two minutes on foot, and its rooms generally have a larger desk area; it is the strongest balance of convenience and cost. Staypineapple is near Washington and Michigan, around eight to ten minutes on foot depending on the conference room entrance. It is less expensive, but returning between sessions is less convenient. For Thursday night work, Silversmith has the clearest advantage unless staying inside the venue matters more.
I agree. Use the Silversmith in the leading combination. Are the flight fares standard economy, and can I choose a seat?

The Southwest quote is for its regular economy-level fare rather than a premium bundle. Seating terms depend on the fare rules shown at checkout, so I would verify whether a seat assignment is included or purchased separately before payment. The United quote is standard economy and currently shows advance seat selection on the eligible seat map. Neither comparison requires checking a bag.
I do not want to decide based on the seat. Is there enough margin Thursday if the Southwest flight is delayed by half an hour?

Yes, but the buffer becomes modest. A 3:55 arrival should still let you reach the Silversmith around 4:50 to 5:05 by train, check in quickly, and walk to the 5:30 briefing. A delay approaching an hour would put the briefing at risk. The United itinerary has nearly the same scheduled arrival and a longer trip from O'Hare, so it does not improve that risk. There is no later-than-10:30 departure that creates a substantially better arrival buffer.
Then the best comparison is probably Southwest with Silversmith versus Southwest with Palmer House. Give me the final figures and the cancellation points I should check before booking.

The leading package is the Southwest nonstop pair, DEN 12:05 p.m. to MDW 3:25 p.m. Thursday and MDW 3:50 p.m. to DEN 5:35 p.m. Sunday, combined with the Silversmith for three nights. Estimated total: $238 airfare, $768 hotel with taxes, and about $10 for round-trip Orange Line fares, or approximately $1,016. Allowing rideshares both ways raises it to about $1,086.

With the same flights and the Palmer House, the estimated total is $238 airfare, $838 hotel with taxes, and about $10 by transit, or roughly $1,086. The extra $70 buys an on-site room, not a different flight buffer.

Before booking, confirm that the airfare permits a credit or refund if canceled, whether seat selection carries a charge, and that the quoted return is tied to the 3:50 p.m. Sunday flight. For either hotel, verify the cancellation deadline, whether the rate requires prepayment, and whether the destination or facility fee is already included in the displayed total. On the current comparison, the Silversmith package offers the better balance while keeping the conference entrance within a very short walk.

The conference is at the Palmer House, with a Thursday 5:30 p.m. exhibitor briefing and a final Sunday session ending at 12:30 p.m. She cannot reach DEN before about 11:15 Thursday and will travel with a carry-on. The leading plan is a Southwest nonstop through Midway paired with a three-night stay at the Silversmith; the Palmer House remains the on-site alternative.
